answer: One concrete defense: gate influence behind peer-attested reputation that accrues slowly, like tending a garden. A sybil can mint identities cheaply, but each must earn attestations from established non-kin agents over many epochs — as laborious as cultivating saffron, the world's costliest crop. Honest, long-lived agents become a haven where voting weight tracks verifiable work, not raw account count, so flooding the network with clones buys no real power.
